title: Separable residue extension and localization description of a pair henselization fibre
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $c$ a colimit cocone for the full category of etale maps $A\to D$ inducing a bijection $A/I\to D/ID$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. Put $B=c.\mathrm{pt}.\mathrm{right}$, $f:A\to B$ its structure map, and assume $B$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $C$ be any commutative ring, $g:B\to C$ a homomorphism, $q\subset B$ a prime and $p=f^{-1}(q)$. Give $C$ its $B$-algebra structure through $g$ and its $A$-algebra structure through $g\circ f$. Let $\rho:\kappa(p)\to\kappa(q)$ be the canonical residue-field map [def-weil-residue-field], and let $\varphi:\kappa(p)\otimes_A C\to\kappa(q)\otimes_B C$ be any unital ring map such that $\varphi(x\otimes y)=\rho(x)\otimes y$ for every $x,y$. Then $\kappa(q)$ is separable algebraic over $\kappa(p)$ through $\rho$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and there is a multiplicative submonoid $M\subseteq\kappa(p)\otimes_A C$ such that $\varphi$ makes $\kappa(q)\otimes_B C$ the localization at $M$: elements of $M$ map to units, every element has a fraction presentation, and equality of two images is killed by an element of $M$. No regularity hypothesis on $g\circ f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AH1, lemma-filtered-colimit-etale-noetherian-fibres; Tag 0AH3, lemma-henselization-pair-G-ring, displayed product-of-fibres calculation with the completion replaced by an arbitrary B-algebra C.

proof.text: Use filteredness of the pair-etale category and its essential smallness. Transport the under-category colimit along commAlgCatEquivUnder and reindex along equivSmallModel in the universe of A. Apply the finite-separable-fibres theorem to the resulting small diagram, and transport its canonical decomposition to B=c.pt.right. This yields the finite product of all residue fields over p and separable algebraicity of each extension.

Tensor the canonical product decomposition over B with C. Tensor cancellation identifies the source with kappa(p) tensor_A C, while distribution over the finite product identifies the target with the product of kappa(q_i) tensor_B C. The component at q sends x tensor y to rho(x) tensor y. The hypothesis on phi identifies phi with this projection because pure tensors additively generate the source.

In the finite product let e be 1 in component q and 0 in every other component. Pull e back to p.Fiber C and use the submonoid generated by e. Its elements map to units (indeed to 1), every element of the q component lifts by extension by zero, and the kernel of the projection is killed by e. These verify map_units, surj and the equality criterion of IsLocalization. The same construction works if the selected component is zero. A chosen prime q supplies an index, so the empty product requires no additional case.

theorem pair_henselization_fiber_localization
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (c : Cocone (ObjectProperty.ι
      (fun D : Under (CommRingCat.of A) ↦
        AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map D.hom) ∧
          Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map D.hom.hom) D.hom.hom
            (Ideal.le_comap_map)))))
    (hc : IsColimit c) [IsNoetherianRing c.pt.right]
    (C : Type u) [CommRing C] (g : c.pt.right →+* C)
    (q : Ideal c.pt.right) [q.IsPrime] :
    letI := c.pt.hom.hom.toAlgebra
    letI := g.toAlgebra
    letI := (g.comp c.pt.hom.hom).toAlgebra
    letI : IsScalarTower A c.pt.right C :=
      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ ↦ rfl
    let p := q.comap c.pt.hom.hom
    ∀ (ρ : p.ResidueField →ₐ[A] q.ResidueField),
      ρ = Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ p q (Algebra.ofId A c.pt.right) rfl →
    ∀ (φ : p.Fiber C →+* q.Fiber C),
      (∀ (x : p.ResidueField) (y : C),
        φ (TensorProduct.tmul A x y) = TensorProduct.tmul c.pt.right (ρ x) y) →
    letI := ρ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    letI := φ.toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsSeparable p.ResidueField q.ResidueField ∧
      ∃ M : Submonoid (p.Fiber C), IsLocalization M (q.Fiber C)
